Commentary.Commentary: We are back! The players stride out to the middle after receiving a pep talk from Kraigg Brathwaite. Alex Lees and Zak Crawley are the openers for England. Kemar Roach to open the bowling for West Indies. Let's go...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

England now have around 15 overs to bat today and we probably will see them get their ODI mode out. Windies on the other hand, will probably look for a few wickets. It has been quite a dull day so far but we can well be in for some entertainment in the last hour or so.

Credit to the England bowlers, despite for being out there for so long, the energy levels just never went down. There was nothing on offer for them from the wicket but they still kept trying. Each of their bowlers had good economy rates to show for as they were very disciplined. Stokes though was the one who was causing a lot of problems. He was relentless with his lines and length. Leach did well too. Saqib and Fisher showed a lot of promise. Woakes will be happy with the lines and lengths he bowled and he got success as well. Jack Leach also became the first England bowler to bowl 69-plus overs in the first innings of a Test match since 1992 and fittingly ended the West Indies' innings. England in the end will be relieved and pleased they have managed to bowl out the hosts.

Finally, West Indies’ marathon innings comes to an end! They will be pleased with their effort as they have given themselves a chance of saving this Test now. This innings for them was about their skipper and their vice captain. Apart from the two, nobody really had a significant contribution. It was the 183 run stand between the two which bailed the Windies out of trouble. Both scored tons and led from the front for their side. Had there been more from the rest, Windies might have just taken the lead.

Credit to the England bowlers who have bowled with a lot of energy despite the amount of time they have spent out there. Also, the wicket has also started to play tricks now. They would hope to take the remaining two quickly after the break. Windies on the other hand, will hope the lower order adds as many runs as possible. England on the other hand, continued to toil hard! The wicket seemed to have flatten even more as there was absolutely nothing in it for the bowlers. They though did manage to keep it tight but wickets is what they were looking for and they got just the one on the bowling of Stokes who probably was the pick of the bowlers in this session. They will need to continue to be patient and hope there is some sort of a collapse. At present we really do not see that happening. Stay tuned for another important session which will begin at 10.40 pm IST (5.10 pm GMT).

That is a solid session for the Windies! We said the first session could well dictate as to which was this game is going and for now, it seems like it is heading towards a draw. The hosts lost just the one wicket and have got the deficit down to just around 150. Both Joseph and Brathwaite showed great resistance early on and added above 50 before Joseph fell. Holder then has showed good solidness to hang in there with Brathwaite. More of the same is what they would want after the break.

PITCH REPORT - Mark Butcher is near the pitch. He says that there's an area which is crumbly and there's a good bare patch in the middle. Tells that there's plenty of rough but it is a long way outside off stump for the right-handers, but most of it is around the bowler's landing area. Mentions that if the batters are absolutely intent on staying in and not taking risks, it's gonna be hard work for the bowlers.

Dan Lawrence is down for a chat. He says if you offered him 90 odd at the start of the day, he would have taken it but he is disappointed he did not get to a ton. Adds he is happy to get his team into a good position. States if he did not hit those boundaries it might have been different, it is a good wicket to bat on and he should have left it alone (stroke that got him out) but Stokes got his ton next day and it turned out well. Reckons a couple of batters who might have not played him might be uncomfortable with his action, he tries to spin it hard and he might not always bowl good balls.

Jermaine Blackwood is up for a chat. Blackwood says when he got to the crease he was told by the skipper to get to a start, he knew if he got to a start he could go big. Adds the wicket is not easy to just come in and score and it was a crucial knock and he enjoyed batting with Brathwaite. States it is important to get past the follow-on and the first hour will be crucial and that is where they’ll need to be good.

Weather update - The news from the middle is that the rains have been on and off but right now, the good news is that it is not raining. The covers were on earlier but now they are coming off. The groundstaff are working on the pitch and if the rain does not arrive again, the play will begin at 7.45 pm IST (2.15 pm GMT). Stay tuned!

The visitors on the other hand, might feel if they do get Kraigg Brathwaite, it could well trigger into a collapse. They would love a lead of around 150 as they can surely push for a win after that. They would dearly hope the wicket deteriorates a lot more.

The hosts are still 20 runs a drift from avoiding the follow-on. That though should not be an issue with the amount of wickets left. They though need to keep doing the good work and one believes Brathwaite holds the key. He needs to continue his innings and hope the rest give him able support. They are doing well for now but it is a new day and things can change quickly.

A lot of will, determination, patience and grittyness was on display by the Windies skipper and vice captain. Courtesy the two, this Test also seems to be heading towards a draw, it will be the 4th draw if that happens in 6 Tests in recent times. However, the slow going by the hosts means England are still well and truly capable of sneaking in a win if they manage to get wickets quickly. The first session could be one which kind of indicates which way the game is heading into.

Jermaine Blackwood is up for a quick chat. He says that he is happy with his performance today and after a slow start, it got easier for batting. Adds that he and Brathwaite just looked to stay out there for as long as possible and he is pleased with his effort. On being asked about his dismissal, he says that he completely misjudged that one as he thought the ball was bouncing much more than it did. About that fiery encounter with Stokes, he says that he likes playing against Stokes and has been doing so since the under-19 days and loves a bit of banter as well.

West Indies will be slightly disappointed as they lost Blackwood late in the evening and they know they are way behind in this match. The good news is they have their skipper, Kraigg Brathwaite out. Just like England, West Indies captain and vice-captain both scored centuries and would have loved the partnership to continue but the slight lapse of concentration saw the stand of 183 collapse. West Indies are still 219 runs behind in this match and it will take some effort from them to get a positive result out of this match with just two days remaining. The same goes for England as well who need a flurry of wickets at the start of Day 4 for any chance of winning from here.

England started the session on a high and they end on the front foot as well. A tiring day for the tourists but they will be happy to get the big wicket of Blackwood just near the end of the day. The lines and lengths were good from England today, Leach and Saqib Mahmood precisely as the latter got the wicket of Blackwood but that turned out to be a no ball while Foakes had a stumping chance off Leach but he too fumbled in his job and that helped Brathwaite survive. England would have loved the wicket of Brathwaite as well but the tiredness showed up as the day progressed.

Session summary: 28 overs / 82 runs / 0 wickets. Well, the hosts have certainly turned things around here in the second session. The captain and the vice-captain have stitched together a partnership of 95 runs, both going past the individual 50-run mark and have frustrated the English bowlers completely. They are still 311 runs behind but they will be feeling much better after that session and given the pitch isn't doing much and the new ball coming onto the bat nicely, the hosts might even look to keep a steady flow of runs in the final session. England need inspiration from somewhere as they have let the advantage slip and even though Jack Leach has kept up his good work, the pacers need to step up a bit more. If they do not try to be a bit more aggressive, they could be out there in the field for a lot longer and this Test match will seem to head towards another draw. West Indies seem to be in a spot of bother here and require a lot of concentration out there in the middle in order to firstly survive the follow on. Skipper Kraigg Brathwaite has been solid and hasn't looked to give away his wicket even once but runs have been hard to come by in the morning session and the pressure is mounting. Shamarh Brooks did give ample support to his skipper but got out in the 30s while playing at a loose ball. The man in form, Nkrumah Bonner though got bogged down from the start and ended up having a lapse in concentration. Brathwaite is still batting out there on 44 and he has the vice-captain, Jermaine Blackwood alongside him. Blackwood has already got lucky once and will have to be careful when he comes back out to bat. The key for the hosts will be to bat through the next session and then take it from there. Will the Windies bat for a second time today? Or will the English bowlers get frustrated by Brathwaite and co? An exciting session awaits. The post-Lunch session will start at 10.10 pm IST (4.40 pm GMT). Do join us then.

Well, it's been an engrossing first session on Day 3. West Indies scored just 43 runs and lost a couple of wickets in 27 overs. They still trail by a mammoth 393 runs. The visitors were the ones who came out with intent and Jack Leach was used right from the start. He proved to be useful as he picked up an early wicket as well. This got the visitors going but even after some good probing by the pacers, wickets were hard to come by. Finally, after some patience and perseverance, Ben Stokes did provide the breakthrough and that too a big one of Nkrumah Bonner. Stokes could have and should have had two but England didn't review an LBW decision which if they did would have seen Blackwood being sent back to the pavillion. All in all, they will be pleased with their efforts and right at the end of the session, Saqib Mahmood even got the ball to reverse.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree is pitchside and is assessing the playing conditions. Badree mentions that the weather cleared out pretty soon and there's going to be an uninterrupted day of action. Mentions that there are some cracks developing as we go on. Leach mentioned that he would want to bowl wicket to wicket and that's the way it should be on this pitch and if there's a bit of turn, the hosts will have a big challenge in front of them.

Jack Leach is up for a quick chat. Jack says that there's a little bit of turn there and it's a slow wicket. Adds that he enjoys bowling from the top end and go against the breeze and will look to carry on today as well. Also adds that it's just about hitting the right areas and staying patient. Mentions that he wants to keep the wickets in play and beat both the edges.

Shamarh Brooks is down for a chat. Brooks says he had to wait his turn but is happy to be back home and get the chance, will look to make the most of it. He adds that it was quite challenging as they were out in the field for almost 2 days but him and Kraig just looked to stay positive and score runs as well. Mentions that Leach got some turn and everyone knows how dangerous Stokes can be.

There has been a bit of rain around in the morning but the forecast looks good for the rest of the day. The massive news though came from the English camp. In a statement, it was revealed that Mark Wood will fly back home and see a specialist and for now he will be on an indefinite break from cricket which means he will miss the entirety of the upcoming Indian T20 League. We wish him the speediest of recoveries.

The pitch is not giving much assistance to the pacers but spinners started to get some turn in the last session of Day 2 and it is expected to get more friendly for the spinners as well. Jack Leach bowled tight lines and asked some questions but Brathwaite in particular negotiated well. Still 436 runs behind, West Indies will hope to start the day on a positive note while England will look to create some early inroads and take control of the match. The first session coming up in a bit.

Hello and a warm welcome to Day 3 of the coverage between West Indies and England. The hosts are off to a great start after being asked to tackle the last one hour on Day 2. Despite losing John Campbell early on, skipper Kraigg Brathwaite and Shamarh Brooks showed good composure and also scored runs at a decent rate. They’ll hope to start the day in the same fashion.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Earlier it was carnage from Root and Stokes as they both scored centuries. Stokes in particular played an entertaining innings and scored in quick time as well. Then, Woakes and Foakes combined and helped England post a total excess of 500. In reply, West Indies lost a wicket early but Brathwaite and Brooks look solid after that. The moving day will be very crucial as England will look for early wickets while the host will hope these two to start in the same fashion as they ended. Day 3 will start at 7.30 pm IST (2 pm GMT). But the build up will begin much early. So, do join us for the same. Till then, Adios.

Ben Stokes is up for a quick chat. He says that it was good to be out there and he capitalized on the good work laid out by Dan Lawrence and Root and once he got in he just tried to score as many runs as possible. Adds that it is important to identify the right situation and when the platform was laid, he tried to get the game moving quickly so that they could have a pop at the end with the ball. Mentions that surprisingly the pitch has changed late and hopes they can get wickets early non Day 3. About his century, he adds that with everything that's going on in his personal life in the past couple of years, it was a memorable century.

It was a dream debut for Matthew Fisher as he got the solitary wicket of the Windies innings. The other bowlers were tight in their lengths and lines as well. Leach bowled some superb deliveries but he was well mediated by the hosts. It started spinning more later in the day and looks like Leach will be very important to get a breakthrough on the moving day.

A decent last session and both the teams will be happy at the end of Day 2. West Indies were off to a brilliant start but they soon lost Campbell. Drinks! As we head into the final hour's play on Day 2, the players take a drinks break. It has been a good contest between bat and bat at the start of the Windies innings and the debutant Matthew Fisher has been the most effective bowler, picking up a wicket of his second delivery in Test cricket. Jack Leach too has looked dangerous and has got the ball to turn but a flurry of boundaries from Kraigg Brathwaite and Shamarh Brooks has seen them muster up a few runs as well. Really interesting to see now as to who heads into Day 3 with the advantage. Also, Ben Stokes is introduced into the attack.

NOT OUT! A foot forward and that might have been a good catch. Fisher goes wide of the crease and angles a full ball, around off. Brooks closes his bat face slightly as he tries to defend on the leg side but gets an outside edge to second slip where Crawley gets his hands low to take it but he seems to have not taken it cleanly. The catch is taken upstairs and the replay shows the ball was grounded.

Is that a clean catch? Everyone on the ground seems it is but the man who took, Zak Crawley doesn't seem as excited as everyone else. The decision is sent upstairs and the soft signal is NOT OUT. The third umpire checks it from a few different angles and concludes that as Crawley took the catch, the ball got grounded a bit. No conclusive evidence to overturn the on-field call and Brooks survives.
